requirements.title: TimelineItem is the single persisted unit of a conversation, with id, optional turnID, date and a tagged content union
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:4-15 struct TimelineItem - Codable, Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable; fields id: String, turnID: UUID?, date: Date, content: Content; init defaults id = UUID().uuidString and date = .now
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:17-26 enum Content - the eight cases the timeline can hold
requirements.preconditions: A thread document is being built in memory or decoded from disk.
requirements.action: The runtime appends or decodes a timeline item.
requirements.expected_result: Every item carries exactly four stored fields: id (String, defaulting to a fresh UUID string), turnID (UUID or null), date (Date, defaulting to now) and content, which is exactly one of user, assistant, reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd. requirements.windows_path: A discriminated-union record type in the Windows model layer, serialized with the same key names and the same single-key-object shape for the union, so a thread written by either build round-trips.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: encode/decode round-trip against a pinned JSON fixture per content case

requirements.title: Attachment identifies a file by path and mime type, is an image when the mime type starts with image/, and hands providers base64 images that are downscaled past 2000 pixels
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:89-97 struct Attachment - id = UUID(), name, path, mimeType; url is URL(fileURLWithPath: path); isImage is mimeType.hasPrefix("image/")

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:102-111 Attachment.base64Images - `@concurrent`; compactMap over attachments; `guard attachment.isImage, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: attachment.url) else { return nil }`; `let downscaled = downscaledJPEG(data)`; `var sent = attachment`; `if downscaled != nil { sent.mimeType = "image/jpeg" }`; `return (sent, (downscaled ?? data).base64EncodedString())`
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:113-137 `private static let maxPixelSize = 2000` and downscaledJPEG, specified in PR-CHAT-190

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:228-232 `for (image, base64) in await Attachment.base64Images(input.images)` with `"media_type": .string(image.mimeType)`; the other callers are DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:177 and DroppyCode/Services/Providers/OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1223
requirements.preconditions: A message carries attachments.
requirements.action: The UI or the provider path asks whether an attachment is an image, or asks for the base64 images.
requirements.expected_result: isImage is a literal prefix test on the mimeType string against "image/", never on the file extension. base64Images reads each image's bytes off the main actor and silently skips any attachment whose bytes cannot be read, returning only the pairs that succeeded, in the original order. For each image it tries downscaledJPEG (PR-CHAT-190): when that returns data, the pair carries that JPEG's base64 and a copy of the attachment whose mimeType is "image/jpeg"; otherwise it carries the original bytes' base64 and the attachment unchanged. The stored attachment is never modified; only the returned copy changes.
side_effects: base64Images reads each image file from disk
An image more than 2000 pixels on its longest side is decoded and re-encoded as a JPEG in memory
requirements.persistence: id, name, path and mimeType are persisted with the message.
failure_cases: A file that cannot be read is dropped from the result with no error and no notice.
An image ImageIO cannot read, or whose JPEG encoding fails, is sent with its original bytes and mime type, with no error and no notice.
requirements.windows_path: URL(fileURLWithPath:) becomes a Windows absolute path; the stored path is the platform path as captured. Base64 encoding and any downscaling must run off the UI thread: the source comment records that a photo is megabytes and its string a third larger again. The returned copy's mime type must follow the bytes actually sent (image/jpeg after a downscale), because the Claude session sends it as the image's media_type (ClaudeSession.swift:228-232).
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fixture directory holding one unreadable path, one image at most 2000 pixels on its longest side and one larger image, asserting order, skipped entries, returned bytes and returned mime types
requirements.b2_change: B1 Timeline.swift:99-105 base64Images returned `(attachment, data.base64EncodedString())` -> B2 Timeline.swift:102-111 returns `(sent, (downscaled ?? data).base64EncodedString())`, with `sent.mimeType = "image/jpeg"` whenever `downscaledJPEG(data)` (B2 :120-137) produced a JPEG, so images above maxPixelSize = 2000 (B2 :114) reach providers downscaled. isImage and the silent skip of unreadable files are unchanged.

requirements.title: Tool output is trimmed to a 60000-byte ceiling by replacing the head with a single ellipsis and keeping the last 30000 bytes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:169 static let outputLimit = 60_000
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:181-189 appendOutput appends then trims; setOutput replaces then trims
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:196-199 trimOutput - guard output.utf8.count > Self.outputLimit; output = "…" + String(output.suffix(Self.outputLimit / 2))
requirements.preconditions: A tool call is streaming or has just received its whole output.
requirements.action: appendOutput or setOutput is called.
requirements.expected_result: While the output's UTF-8 byte count is at most 60000 it is kept whole. Above that the output becomes the single character U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS followed by the last 30000 Characters of the current output. Note that the guard counts UTF-8 bytes while suffix counts Characters, so the trimmed result can still exceed 60000 bytes for non-ASCII output; this is the shipped behavior.
requirements.persistence: The trimmed value is what is stored in the item and written to disk.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the byte-count guard and the Character-count suffix exactly, including the unit mismatch. Windows string indices are UTF-16 code units: suffix must be taken over grapheme clusters, not code units, or a surrogate pair is split.
requirements.verification_method: unit with an ASCII case, a CJK case and an emoji case at the boundary

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:862-889 refreshViewport - skipped without a viewport height or while a nudge is under way, deferred while scrolling; a nudge is begun and then restored, restoring the end when the reader was pinned within a point; with no scroll view but a pinned reader and travel above one point, the offset itself is moved one point up and then back to the end on the next main-queue turn; with nothing to scroll and the last block unseen the stack is rebuilt instead

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1210-1235 noteNudgeSeen and restoreNudge - the nudge advances when the scroll view reports geometry; the restore waits up to four frames, moves back to the recorded origin, runs the completion, then clears the phase one frame later

requirements.windows_path: Only needed where the list virtualizes against a remembered viewport; if the Windows list derives its range from the live offset, state that this requirement collapses to a no-op rather than porting the nudge.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1804-1811 `static let firstPaint = 3`, `static let initial = 24`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:713-720 a thread switch sets `windowStartID = nil`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:257-268 loadEarlier - with count TimelineWindow.initial the target is `count.map { max(0, blocks.count - $0) }`, the block count minus 24 floored at zero, and `guard target < start else { return }` leaves the window unanchored when that target is not before the fallback start

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:595-603 `.task(id: runtime.threadID)` inside timelineScroll(blocks:...) sleeps 250 ms and then calls `loadEarlier(in: blocks, to: TimelineWindow.initial)` with the `blocks` its closure captured
requirements.preconditions: windowStartID is nil (a thread just opened or switched to, before the 250 ms load anchors it) or names a block that is no longer in the conversation.
requirements.action: The timeline body runs.
requirements.expected_result: The window is the newest min(3, block count) blocks, and the earlier-messages pill counts the rest as hidden. While unanchored, an appended block moves the window along with the end, so it stays the newest three. A thread whose block list, as captured by the thread task when it started (the `blocks` passed to timelineScroll when `.task(id: runtime.threadID)` began), holds three blocks or fewer stays unanchored after the 250 ms load, because that load computes its target (that captured count minus 24, floored at zero) and the fallback start from the captured list, and the target is not before the start; it stays so until a page load or a jump sets the anchor. A stale anchor is not cleared by the lookup: it simply stops matching.
requirements.windows_path: Compute the fallback on every pass rather than storing it, and leave a stale anchor id in place, exactly as the source does.
requirements.verification_method: unit over the window-start function with a nil anchor, a present anchor and a removed anchor; interaction test opening a two-block thread and streaming two more blocks, asserting the pill appears with 1 hidden

requirements.title: Conversation fonts are the plain system text styles, with headline semibold unless a weight is given, and no chat zoom
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatFont.swift:3-10 `extension Font { static func chat(_ style: Font.TextStyle, weight: Font.Weight? = nil, design: Font.Design = .default) -> Font { let resolvedWeight = weight ?? (style == .headline ? .semibold : nil); let font = Font.system(style, design: design); return resolvedWeight.map { font.weight($0) } ?? font } }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatFont.swift:4-5 the doc comment: A text style in the conversation's own weight, so the chat reads as the app's type and not a second scale. The app-wide zoom scales the window, not the type.

Callers at B2, for example DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ChatBadge.swift:28 `.font(.chat(.callout, weight: .medium))`, TimelineRows.swift:1370 `.font(.chat(.caption))` and TimelineRows.swift:2151 `.font(.chat(.caption, design: .monospaced))`
DroppyCode/UI/Common/AppZoom.swift:18-26 AppZoomModifier scales the window content with `content.scaleEffect(scale, anchor: .topLeading)`
requirements.preconditions: A chat view asks for a conversation font.
requirements.action: Font.chat(style, weight:, design:) is evaluated.
requirements.expected_result: The result is the system font for the text style, in the given design, with the given weight; with no weight given, headline is semibold and every other style keeps its own weight. The size is always the text style's own size: no setting or environment value changes it, and the app-wide zoom scales the whole window content rather than the type, so the conversation and the rest of the app share one type scale.
requirements.windows_path: One text-style table for the whole app; the conversation carries no second scale and no zoom factor. Per ED-059 each text style takes the size of upstream's B1 table, in Inter, and in Cascadia Mono where the design is .monospaced (OD-0009): largeTitle 26 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:47), title 22 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:48), title2 17 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:49), title3 15 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:50), headline and body 13 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:51), callout 12 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:52), subheadline 11 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:53), footnote, caption and caption2 10 (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:54). The sizes are fixed per style and scale only through the app zoom (DroppyCode/UI/Common/AppZoom.swift); no B2 file restates them, so visual size parity stays UNVERIFIED under OD-0001.
requirements.verification_method: unit over the font helper for every text style with and without an explicit weight, plus a capture comparison showing a chat row and a chrome label at the same text style render at the same size
